question: If \(x=\frac{a}{b},\) \(a\ne b,\) and \(b\ne0,\) then \(\dfrac{a+b}{a-b}=\)
solution:
Since \(x=a/b\), divide both the numerator and denominator by \(b\) to make that ratio appear. This is valid because \(b\ne0\):
\[
\frac{a+b}{a-b}
=\frac{a/b+1}{a/b-1}
=\frac{x+1}{x-1}.
\]
Moreover, \(x-1=(a-b)/b\ne0\), so the resulting fraction is defined under the original assumptions. The answer is \(\boxed{\frac{x+1}{x-1}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
